data.name: Table_Overview
data.value: The <fdcp-table> component wraps the GC Design System <gcds-table> by parsing a List<T> of row models and rendering each item as a table row. Columns are resolved from [TableColumnDefinition]-annotated properties on the row model. Columns can also be supplied explicitly via column-definitions. Custom cell content (links, buttons, etc.) is rendered via <template slot="cell:fieldName">.

data.name: Card_Overview
data.value: The <fdcp-card> component provides a flexible and extensible content container inspired by Bootstrap cards, designed with Government of Canada Design System (GCDS) styling. It includes options for headers, footers, images, and various contextual background colors.

data.name: Modal_Basic_Text
data.value: <gcds-text>Modals provide a focused, interruptive space for short, high-priority tasks or confirmations that must be completed before users continue their workflow.</gcds-text>

data.name: Modal_WhenToUse_1
data.value: The user must make a brief, time-sensitive decision or acknowledgement.

data.name: Modal_WhenToUse_2
data.value: The task requires 1–2 clear actions and benefits from focused attention.

data.name: Modal_WhenToUse_3
data.value: Inline content would disrupt the page structure or cause confusion.

data.name: Modal_WhenToUse_4
data.value: The decision is contextual to the current page and does not require navigation.

data.name: Modal_Accessibility_Do_1
data.value: 2.4.3 Focus Order: Focus moves into the modal and returns to the button or trigger that opened it. Background content cannot be interacted with and is out of focus.

data.name: Modal_Accessibility_Do_2
data.value: 2.4.7 Focus Visible: Every interactive element must show a visible focus outline.

data.name: Modal_Accessibility_Do_3
data.value: 2.1.1 Keyboard: Fully functional with a keyboard, including closing the modal with the Escape key.

data.name: Modal_Accessibility_Do_4
data.value: 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap: If focus is trapped, the user must be able to exit the trap.

data.name: Modal_Accessibility_Do_5
data.value:
1.3.1 Info and Relationships: Uses ARIA roles, labels, and descriptions, i.e.:
  • the modal uses role="dialog";
  • the title is linked using aria-labelledby;
  • and, the description is linked using aria-describedby.

data.name: Modal_Accessibility_Do_6
data.value: 1.4.3 Contrast Minimum: Text and essential UI elements must meet minimum contrast ratios (3:1). The white modal box sits on a darkened backdrop, ensuring strong contrast.

data.name: Modal_WhenNotToUse_1
data.value: The content is long, complex, multi-step, or requires detailed reading.

data.name: Modal_WhenNotToUse_2
data.value: Users must compare information or reference other parts of the interface.

data.name: Modal_WhenNotToUse_3
data.value: Scrolling or extensive interaction would be required within the modal.

data.name: Modal_WhenNotToUse_4
data.value: The interruption is unnecessary and could be handled inline or on a dedicated page.

data.name: Modal_Notes_4
data.value: Modal content should be wrapped in <div slot="body"> and <div slot="footer"> elements

data.name: Modal_Notes_1
data.value: Modals require unique IDs when multiple are used on the same page

data.name: Modal_Notes_3
data.value: Use static-backdrop for modals that require user action

data.name: Modal_Notes_2
data.value: Session modals automatically handle timeout warnings and session extension

data.name: Badge_Purpose
data.value: Badges highlight short, categorical pieces of information such as status, priority, or metadata. They help users quickly scan and differentiate key details.

data.name: Badge_WhenToUse_1
data.value: You need to call out a small piece of status- or category-based information.

data.name: Badge_WhenToUse_2
data.value: You want to add supplemental context to headings, labels, lists, cards, or tables.

data.name: Badge_WhenToUse_3
data.value: Users need to distinguish between types or states at a glance.

data.name: Badge_WhenNotToUse_1
data.value: The information requires explanation or is longer than a short phrase.

data.name: Badge_WhenNotToUse_2
data.value: The badge is the only way a user can understand critical information.

data.name: Badge_WhenNotToUse_3
data.value: Too many badges together create cognitive overload or visual clutter.

data.name: Badge_Accessibility_Do_1
data.value: Use text or iconography in addition to colour to convey meaning.

data.name: Badge_Accessibility_Do_2
data.value: Meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast requirements for text and background.

data.name: Badge_Accessibility_Do_3
data.value: Use consistent colour semantics aligned to system tokens (e.g., green for success, red for warnings, grey for neutral metadata).

data.name: Badge_Accessibility_Do_4
data.value: Remain readable and operable at 200% zoom and on small screens.

data.name: Badge_Accessibility_Do_5
data.value: Use coloured variants only when colour supports a clear distinction— e.g., green for success, red for warnings, grey for neutral metadata. But ALWAYS pair it with a meaningful icon or shape.

data.name: Badge_Accessibility_DoNot_1
data.value: Use a red badge with the label "Error" and a grey badge with the label "Error" interchangeably if colour is the only difference.

data.name: Badge_Accessibility_DoNot_2
data.value: Use colour alone to communicate categories such as priority levels.

data.name: Badge_UxBestPractices_1
data.value: Keep badges brief (one–two words) and place them close to the element they describe.

data.name: Badge_UxBestPractices_2
data.value: Use consistently across the product for the same meaning or category.

data.name: Badge_UxBestPractices_3
data.value: Avoid stacking multiple badges unless each communicates clearly distinct information.

data.name: Badge_UxBestPractices_4
data.value: Follow system spacing, sizing, and colour guidance to maintain visual harmony.

data.name: Stepper_WithStatus_Text
data.value:
This implementation adds a small status badge next to a step label (for example, “Done” or “Not required”). Set StatusBadgeLabel and choose a StatusBadgeStyle to match your UI semantics. You can also invert the badge style when you need more emphasis or contrast. This pattern can also be used when one or more steps are identified as "not required" because a user’s earlier choices make those steps not applicable. To support clarity, consistency, and accessibility:
  • Skipped steps must visually include a label/badge such as “N/A” or “Not required” as shown in the design system pattern.
  • A notice at the top of the page is recommended to inform users that steps have been skipped and why. Here is an example: Steps shown as N/A were skipped because your previous answers provided enough information to move ahead.

data.name: Stepper_Accessibility_Do_1
data.value:
Clearly identify skipped steps:
  • Given a step has been skipped due to previous answers
  • Then the step must display a visual badge reading “N/A” or “Not required”
  • And, an accessible label must be present (e.g., “Step 2 not required based on your previous answers”)

data.name: Stepper_Accessibility_Do_2
data.value:
Make skipped steps non-interactive:
  • Given a step is in a skipped state
  • Then, it must not be reachable via keyboard navigation
  • Then, it must not behave like an interactive element (no hover, no click, no focus ring)
  • And, the user must not be able to activate or navigate into skipped steps.

data.name: Stepper_Accessibility_Do_3
data.value:
Announce skipped steps programmatically (A11y):
  • Given a screen-reader user encounters a skipped step
  • Then, the skipped step must announce: “Step X: Skipped: (Optional) This step is not required based on your previous answers.”

data.name: Stepper_Properties_StepperStep_IsHidden
data.value: Optional. Should the step be hidden from display.

data.name: Stepper_Properties_StepperStep_StatusBadgeLabel
data.value: Optional. Label of the status badge.

data.name: Stepper_Properties_StepperStep_StatusBadgeStyle
data.value: Optional. Style of the status badge.

data.name: Stepper_Properties_StepperStep_StatusBadgeStyleInverted
data.value: Optional. Inverted variant of the style of the status badge.

data.name: Table_Basic_Summary
data.value: Table listing employee ID, name, department, and employment status.

data.name: Table_BasicUsage_Text
data.value: Pass a List<T> of row models to the rows attribute — <fdcp-table> renders each item as a table row. Decorate properties on the row model with [TableColumnDefinition] to define them as columns. Columns can also be defined explicitly by passing a List<ColumnDefinition> to column-definitions.See all available properties below. For more examples on filtering and pagination, see the GC Design System table documentation — <fdcp-table> implements these features the same way.

data.name: Table_BasicUsage_GCDSNote
data.value: For more examples on filtering and pagination, see the GC Design System table documentation — <fdcp-table> implements these features the same way.

data.name: Table_WithAnnotations_Text
data.value: Decorate each property you want to display with [TableColumnDefinition]. Use Name and ResourceType to provide a localized column header. Set RowHeader = true to mark a column as the row header, Sort = true to enable sorting, or Slotted = true for custom cell content.

data.name: Table_WithAnnotations_Warning
data.value: Properties without the annotation are excluded from the rendered columns but are still serialized into the page's row data. They remain accessible client-side for data-bind* bindings and JavaScript via element.row.

data.name: Table_WithColumns_Text
data.value: As an alternative, pass a List<ColumnDefinition> to column-definitions to define columns entirely in the controller.

data.name: Table_WithSlots_Text
data.value: Replace any cell's default text output with custom HTML using a named slot: <template slot="cell:fieldName">. Mark the corresponding model property with [TableColumnDefinition(Slotted = true)] so the component renders the slot instead of plain text. Use data-bind* attributes inside the template to bind row values to elements.

data.name: Table_DataBinding_Text
data.value: Inside any <template slot="cell:fieldName">, use the following attributes to populate elements from the current row's data.

data.name: Table_DataBinding_FieldName_Desc
data.value: When using [TableColumnDefinition], this is the camelCase form of the annotated property name (e.g. SubmitterName → {submitterName}). Otherwise, it is whatever field name was explicitly set.

data.name: Table_DataBinding_Bind_Desc
data.value: Sets the element's text content to the value of the named row field.

data.name: Table_DataBinding_Template_Desc
data.value: Builds the element's text content from a template string containing one or more {fieldName} tokens.

data.name: Table_DataBinding_Attr_Desc
data.value: Sets the named HTML attribute to the value of a row field (e.g. data-bind-button-id="{submissionId}").

data.name: Table_DataBinding_TemplateAttr_Desc
data.value: Interpolates one or more {fieldName} tokens into a template string and sets the result as the named HTML attribute (e.g. data-bind-template-href="mailto:{email}").

data.name: Table_WithEmail_Text
data.value: Use data-bind-template-href="mailto:{fieldName}" to build a mailto: link from a row value.

data.name: Table_WithLink_Text
data.value: You can use data-bind-template and data-bind-template-href with {fieldName} tokens to build strings from row field values into the link's text and destination URL.

data.name: Table_WithButton_Text
data.value: Use data-bind-{attribute} to bind a row field to any attribute on the slotted element. For example, data-bind-button-id="{fieldName}" sets the button's button-id from that row field.

data.name: Table_WithButtonLink_Text
data.value: A type="link" button inside the slot navigates like a link. Use data-bind-template-href to supply the destination URL from the current row's data.

data.name: Table_Properties_FdcpTable_Caption
data.value: Accessible name for the table, announced by assistive technologies. Required for WCAG compliance.

data.name: Table_Properties_FdcpTable_CaptionDetail
data.value: Additional descriptive text displayed below the caption.

data.name: Table_Properties_FdcpTable_ColumnDefinitions
data.value: Optional explicit column definitions. When omitted, only properties decorated with [TableColumnDefinition] on the row model are displayed as columns, with the header and behaviour configured directly in the annotation.

data.name: Table_Properties_FdcpTable_Filter
data.value: Enables a keyword filter input above the table to narrow displayed rows.

data.name: Table_Properties_FdcpTable_FilterValue
data.value: Pre-fills the filter input with a default keyword when the table loads. Only applies when filter is true.

data.name: Table_Properties_FdcpTable_PaginationCurrentPage
data.value: The page shown when the table first loads. Only applies when pagination is true.

data.name: Table_Properties_FdcpTable_PaginationSize
data.value: Number of rows displayed per page. Only applies when pagination is true.

data.name: Table_Properties_FdcpTable_PaginationSizeOptions
data.value: Page-size choices available in the pagination control. Include 0 to add an "All" option. Only applies when pagination is true.

data.name: Table_Properties_FdcpTable_Rows
data.value: The server-side collection of row data to display.

data.name: Table_Properties_FdcpTable_Sort
data.value: Enables sorting by clicking column headers. Can also be enabled per-column via ColumnDefinition.Sort or [TableColumnDefinition(Sort = true)].

data.name: Table_Properties_ColumnDef_Alignment
data.value: Controls horizontal alignment of cell content. Values: start (left), center, end (right).

data.name: Table_Properties_ColumnDef_Field
data.value: The camelCase name of the property on the row model that this column maps to.

data.name: Table_Properties_ColumnDef_Header
data.value: The column header label displayed in the table's <thead>.

data.name: Table_Properties_ColumnDef_RowHeader
data.value: Marks each cell in this column as a row header.

data.name: Table_Properties_ColumnDef_Slotted
data.value: Enables custom cell content for this column via <template slot="cell:fieldName">.

data.name: Table_Properties_ColumnDef_Sort
data.value: Enables sorting by this column when clicked.

data.name: Table_Properties_ColumnDef_SortDirection
data.value: Sets the default sort order when the page loads. Values: asc, desc, none. Only applies when Sort is true.

data.name: Table_Properties_Annotation_Text
data.value: [TableColumnDefinition] is required on every property that should appear as a column. Properties without this annotation are automatically excluded from the rendered table but remain accessible on the row data for data-bind* bindings and JavaScript via element.row.

data.name: Table_Properties_Annotation_NameResourceType
data.value: Sets the column header text. Provide a resource key as Name and the resource class as ResourceType for a localized header.

data.name: Table_Properties_Annotation_Alignment
data.value: Controls horizontal alignment of cell content. Values: start (left), center, end (right).

data.name: Table_Properties_Annotation_IsHidden
data.value: Explicitly hides this column from the rendered table even when [TableColumnDefinition] is present.

data.name: Table_Properties_Annotation_Order
data.value: Controls the display order of this column relative to other columns. Columns are rendered in ascending order by this value.

data.name: Table_Properties_Annotation_RowHeader
data.value: Marks each cell in this column as a row header.

data.name: Table_Properties_Annotation_Slotted
data.value: Enables custom slotted cell content for this column.

data.name: Table_Properties_Annotation_Sort
data.value: Enables sorting by this column when clicked.

data.name: Table_Properties_Annotation_SortDirection
data.value: Sets the default sort order when the page loads. Values: asc, desc, none. Only applies when Sort is true.

data.name: Index_TagHelpers_Section_Description
data.value: Quick reference for FDCP and GCDS tag helpers, including what each helper does, key properties, and a minimal usage snippet.

data.name: Table_WithButton_Note
data.value: Note: In this demo, clicking a Delete button logs the row object and its submissionId to the browser console.

data.name: Table_WithButton_SlottedCellContext_Text
data.value: For each slotted cell, the table adds .row and .column properties to the rendered element. .row contains the complete data object for the current row, while .column contains the definition and metadata for the current column.

data.name: Table_WithLink_Note
data.value: Note: In this demo, the link navigates to a page anchor. In a real application, data-bind-template-href="/your/route/{fieldName}" can build the destination URL dynamically from a row value.

data.name: Table_WithButtonLink_Note
data.value: Note: In this demo, the button navigates to a page anchor. In a real application, data-bind-template-href="/your/route/{fieldName}" can build the destination URL dynamically from a row value.

data.name: Table_WithCaptionSlot_Text
data.value: Use <div slot="caption"> to inject custom content into the caption area of the table alongside the caption and caption-detail attributes. This is useful for placing action controls such as buttons directly above the table.

data.name: Table_WithCaptionSlot_Note
data.value: Note: In this demo, clicking the Add submission button logs a message to the browser console.

data.name: Index_Tabs_Description
data.value: Organize related in-page content into accessible tab panels.

data.name: Tabs_Overview
data.value: Tabs let people switch between related panels of content without leaving the current page context.

data.name: Tabs_Purpose
data.value: Use tabs to group peer sections of content where only one section needs to be visible at a time.

data.name: Tabs_WhenToUse_1
data.value: Use tabs when the sections are closely related and people benefit from comparing or switching between them in place.

data.name: Tabs_WhenToUse_2
data.value: Use tabs when each panel can stand on its own and the first tab provides a sensible default view.

data.name: Tabs_WhenNotToUse_1
data.value: Do not use tabs for primary site navigation or page-to-page navigation. Use GCDS navigation components for those patterns.

data.name: Tabs_WhenNotToUse_2
data.value: Do not hide critical tasks, errors, or required instructions in a tab that might not be selected.

data.name: Tabs_Accessibility_Do_1
data.value: Provide a meaningful label on fdcp-tabs so assistive technologies can describe the tab list.

data.name: Tabs_Accessibility_Do_2
data.value: Keep tab labels short and unique so people can understand the available panels quickly.

data.name: Tabs_Accessibility_Do_3
data.value: Make sure each tab panel has enough context when read on its own, because screen reader users may navigate directly between panels.

data.name: Tabs_UxBestPractices_1
data.value: Limit the number of tabs so the tab list remains scannable and works well on small screens.

data.name: Tabs_UxBestPractices_2
data.value: Order tabs by importance or the expected user workflow, with the most useful panel first.

data.name: Tabs_Notes_1
data.value: The component follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern. Left Arrow, Right Arrow, Home, and End move focus; Enter or Space activates the focused tab.

data.name: Tabs_Notes_2
data.value: Tabs are for switching content panels in the current page. For page navigation, use GCDS top navigation, side navigation, or links.

data.name: Tabs_Notes_3
data.value: When load-url is set, the panel content is fetched the first time the tab is selected and then cached for later tab changes.

data.name: Tabs_Properties_Id
data.value: Optional. Unique ID for the tabs component. Used to generate deterministic tab and panel IDs.

data.name: Tabs_Properties_Label
data.value: Accessible label for the tab list.

data.name: Tabs_Properties_SelectedIndex
data.value: Optional. Zero-based index of the tab selected when the page loads. Overrides child active state when valid.

data.name: Tabs_Properties_TabTitle
data.value: Required. Text shown in the tab button.

data.name: Tabs_Properties_TabId
data.value: Optional. Base ID used to generate the child tab and panel IDs.

data.name: Tabs_Properties_TabActive
data.value: Optional. Selects this tab when the page loads if selected-index is not set.

data.name: Tabs_Properties_TabLoadUrl
data.value: Optional. URL that returns an HTML fragment to lazy-load into the panel when the tab is selected.

data.name: Tabs_Basic_Text
data.value: Use nested fdcp-tab elements inside fdcp-tabs to define each tab label and panel content.

data.name: Tabs_Sample_Overview_Content
data.value: Use the overview tab for the most important summary content.

data.name: Tabs_Sample_Details_Content
data.value: Use the details tab for supporting information that belongs in the same context.

data.name: Tabs_Sample_History_Content
data.value: Use the history tab for related changes or previous activity.

data.name: Tabs_LazyContent
data.value: This content was loaded from the server when the tab was selected.

data.name: Modal_Notes_6
data.value: The <fdcp-modal> component handles its WCAG 2.2 accessibility requirements natively.

data.name: Modal_Properties_ModalId
data.value: Unique identifier used to target the modal

data.name: Modal_Properties_State
data.value: Visual and semantic state of the modal (regular, info, or warning)

data.name: Modal_Properties_HideCloseButton
data.value: Hides the close button in the modal header

data.name: Modal_Properties_StaticBackdrop
data.value: Prevents the modal from closing when the backdrop is clicked or the Escape key is pressed

data.name: Modal_BasicStructure_Text
data.value: Renders a standalone modal component. Use <fdcp-modal> in your Razor views to generate a modal dialog.

data.name: Modal_ButtonBehaviour_Text
data.value:
Buttons interact with a modal through a combination of the modal-id attribute and CSS utility classes.
  • modal-id — Set on the trigger button to match the modal-id of the target <fdcp-modal>. This links the button to the correct modal.
  • fdcp-modal-open — Add this class to any button outside the modal to open it when clicked.
  • fdcp-modal-close — Add this class to any button inside the modal (typically in the footer) to close it when clicked.

data.name: Modal_ButtonBehaviour_ProgrammaticText
data.value: For custom interactions, use JavaScript to listen for any event your application requires, find the rendered modal by its modal-id, and toggle its show class. The component detects this class change and automatically applies its focus and accessibility behaviour.

data.name: Modal_Variants_Text
data.value: The modal component supports three state variants — regular, info, and warning — each designed for a different level of urgency or intent.

data.name: Modal_Default_Text
data.value: Used for standard tasks that require user attention or confirmation. It provides a neutral presentation for everyday interactions. This is the default variant and will be applied automatically if no state property is specified.

data.name: Modal_Default_Body
data.value: This is a regular modal, shown with no special state applied.

data.name: Modal_Info_Text
data.value: Delivers important information or context that users should understand before proceeding. It highlights details that support decision-making without implying risk.

data.name: Modal_Info_Body
data.value: This is an info modal, used to highlight helpful or supplementary information for the user.

data.name: Modal_Warning_Text
data.value: Alerts users to high-impact or irreversible actions.

data.name: Modal_Warning_Body
data.value: This is a warning modal, used to alert the user to something that needs their attention before proceeding.

data.name: Modal_Size_Regular_Text
data.value: The regular size suits most everyday interactions and is applied automatically when no size property is specified.

data.name: Modal_Size_Small_Text
data.value: Use the small size for brief confirmations or simple messages that require minimal content.

data.name: Modal_Size_Large_Text
data.value: Use the large size when the content requires more space, such as forms, data tables, or complex layouts.

data.name: Modal_AdditionalProperties_Text
data.value: Beyond the core structure, <fdcp-modal> supports several optional properties to control its behaviour. The example below illustrates scrollable, hide-close-button, and static-backdrop — none of which affect content, only how the modal behaves.

data.name: Modal_Session_Body
data.value: Your session is about to expire!

data.name: Index_Accordion_Description
data.value: Organize related content into expandable sections.

data.name: Accordion_Overview
data.value: The <fdcp-accordion> component organizes related content into expandable sections and provides a control to open or close all sections.

data.name: Accordion_BasicUsage_Text
data.value: The <fdcp-accordion> component groups multiple <gcds-details> components into a dynamic accordion. It includes a button that lets users open all or close all sections. The accordion-id attribute is mandatory.

data.name: Accordion_BasicUsage_AboutService_Text
data.value: Learn about the services available and who is eligible to use them.

data.name: Accordion_BasicUsage_BeforeStart_Text
data.value: Gather the information you need before you begin your request.

data.name: Accordion_BasicUsage_AfterApply_Text
data.value: Find out what happens after you submit your request.

data.name: Accordion_BasicAccordion_Text
data.value: Use a basic accordion to group related information into expandable sections.

data.name: Accordion_AlwaysOpen_Text
data.value: Use the always-open property to allow multiple accordion sections to remain open at the same time.

data.name: Accordion_AlwaysOpen_Eligibility_Text
data.value: Review the eligibility requirements before applying.

data.name: Accordion_AlwaysOpen_RequiredDocuments_Text
data.value: Prepare the documents required to support your application.

data.name: Accordion_ButtonsPosition_Text
data.value: Set buttons-position to top, bottom, or both. This example displays the expand-all and collapse-all buttons above and below the accordion.

data.name: Accordion_ButtonsPosition_SubmitApplication_Text
data.value: Complete and submit the application form.

data.name: Accordion_ButtonsPosition_TrackApplication_Text
data.value: Check the status of your submitted application.

data.name: Accordion_Properties_FdcpAccordion_AccordionId
data.value: Unique identifier for the accordion container. The value is rendered as the container's id and is used to associate the component's client-side behaviour.

data.name: Accordion_Properties_FdcpAccordion_ButtonsPosition
data.value: Controls where the expand-all and collapse-all buttons are displayed. Accepted values are top, bottom, and both.

data.name: Accordion_Properties_FdcpAccordion_AlwaysOpen
data.value: When true, allows multiple accordion sections to remain open at the same time.
